IR.III.A.K1.text: Elements and procedures related to ATC clearances and pilot/controller responsibilities for departure, en route, and arrival phases of flight, including clearance void times.

IR.III.A.K3.text: Lost communication procedures and procedures for flights outside of radar environments.

IR.III.A.R1.text: Less than full understanding of an ATC clearance.

IR.III.A.R2.text: Inappropriate, incomplete, or incorrect ATC clearances.

IR.III.A.R3.text: ATC clearance inconsistent with aircraft performance or navigation capability.

IR.III.A.R4.text: ATC clearance intended for other aircraft with similar call signs.

IR.III.A.S1.text: Correctly copy, read back, interpret, and comply with simulated or actual ATC clearances in a timely manner using standard phraseology as provided in the Aeronautical Information Manual (AIM).

IR.III.A.S2.text: Correctly set communication frequencies, navigation systems (identifying when appropriate), and transponder codes in compliance with the ATC clearance.

IR.III.A.S3.text: Use the current and appropriate paper or electronic navigation publications.

IR.III.A.S4.text: Intercept all courses, radials, and bearings appropriate to the procedure, route, or clearance in a timely manner.

IR.III.A.S5.text: Maintain the applicable airspeed ±10 knots, headings ±10°, altitude ±100 feet; track a course, radial, or bearing within ¾-scale deflection of the course deviation indicator (CDI).

IR.III.A.S6.text: Use single-pilot resource management (SRM) or crew resource management (CRM), as appropriate.

IR.III.A.S7.text: Perform the appropriate checklist items relative to the phase of flight.

IR.III.B.K1.text: Elements related to holding procedures, including reporting criteria, appropriate speeds, and recommended entry procedures for standard, nonstandard, published, and non-published holding patterns.

IR.III.B.R1.text: Recalculating fuel reserves if assigned an unanticipated expect further clearance (EFC) time.

IR.III.B.R2.text: Scenarios and circumstances that could result in minimum fuel or the need to declare an emergency.

IR.III.B.R3.text: Scenarios that could lead to holding, including deteriorating weather at the planned destination.

IR.III.B.R4.text: Holding entry and wind correction while holding.

IR.III.B.S1.text: Use an entry procedure appropriate for a standard, nonstandard, published, or non-published holding pattern.

IR.III.B.S2.text: Change to the holding airspeed appropriate for the altitude when 3 minutes or less from, but prior to arriving at, the holding fix and set appropriate power as needed for fuel conservation.

IR.III.B.S3.text: Recognize arrival at the holding fix and promptly initiate entry into the holding pattern.

IR.III.B.S3a.text: a. Comply with the holding pattern leg length and other restrictions, if applicable, associated with the holding pattern

IR.III.B.S4.text: Maintain airspeed ±10 knots, altitude ±100 feet, selected headings within ±10°, and track a selected course, radial, or bearing within ¾-scale deflection of the course deviation indicator (CDI).

IR.III.B.S5.text: Use proper wind correction procedures to maintain the desired pattern and to arrive over the fix as close as possible to a specified time.

IR.III.B.S6.text: Use a multi-function display (MFD) and other graphical navigation displays, if installed, to monitor position in relation to the desired flightpath during holding.

IR.III.B.S7.text: Comply with ATC reporting requirements and restrictions associated with the holding pattern.

IR.III.B.S8.text: Use single-pilot resource management (SRM) or crew resource management (CRM), as appropriate. 10

IR.IV.A.K1.text: Elements related to attitude instrument flying during straight-and-level flight, climbs, turns, and descents while conducting various instrument flight procedures.

IR.IV.A.K2.text: Interpretation, operation, and limitations of pitch, bank, and power instruments.

IR.IV.A.K3.text: Normal and abnormal instrument indications and operations.

IR.IV.A.R1.text: Situations that can affect physiology and degrade instrument cross-check.

IR.IV.A.R3.text: Flying unfamiliar aircraft or operating with unfamiliar flight display systems and avionics.

IR.IV.A.S1.text: Maintain altitude ±100 feet during level flight, selected headings ±10°, airspeed ±10 knots, and bank angles ±5° during turns.

IR.IV.A.S2.text: Use proper instrument cross-check and interpretation, and apply the appropriate pitch, bank, power, and trim corrections when applicable.

IR.IV.B.K1.text: Procedures for recovery from unusual attitudes in flight.

IR.IV.B.K2.text: Prevention of unusual attitudes, including flight causal, physiological, and environmental factors, and system and equipment failures.

IR.IV.B.K3.text: Procedures available to safely regain visual meteorological conditions (VMC) after flight into inadvertent instrument meteorological conditions or unintended instrument meteorological conditions (IIMC)/(UIMC).

IR.IV.B.K4.text: Appropriate use of automation, if applicable.

IR.IV.B.R1.text: Situations that could lead to loss of control in-flight (LOC-I) or unusual attitudes in-flight (e.g., stress, task saturation, inadequate instrument scan distractions, and spatial disorientation).

IR.IV.B.R6.text: Control input errors, inducing undesired aircraft attitudes.

IR.IV.B.R7.text: Control application solely by reference to instruments.

IR.IV.B.R9.text: Distractions, task prioritization, loss of situational awareness, or disorientation.

IR.IV.B.S1.text: Use proper instrument cross-check and interpretation to identify an unusual attitude (including both nose-high and nose-low) in flight, and apply the appropriate flight control, power input, and aircraft configuration in the correct sequence, to return to a stabilized level flight attitude.

IR.IV.B.S2.text: Use single-pilot resource management (SRM) or crew resource management (CRM), as appropriate. 12

IR.V.A.K1.text: Ground-based navigation (orientation, course determination, equipment, tests, and regulations), including procedures for intercepting and tracking courses and arcs.

IR.V.A.K2.text: Satellite-based navigation (orientation, course determination, equipment, tests, regulations, interference, appropriate use of databases, Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM), and Wide Area Augmentation System (WAAS)), including procedures for intercepting and tracking courses and arcs.

IR.V.A.R1.text: Management of automated navigation and autoflight systems.

IR.V.A.R2.text: Distractions, task prioritization, loss of situational awareness, or disorientation.

IR.V.A.R3.text: Limitations of the navigation system in use.

IR.V.A.S1.text: Tune and identify the navigation facility/program the navigation system and verify system accuracy as appropriate for the equipment installed in the aircraft.

IR.V.A.S10.text: Use single-pilot resource management (SRM) or crew resource management (CRM), as appropriate. 13

IR.V.A.S2.text: Determine aircraft position relative to the navigational facility or waypoint.

IR.V.A.S3.text: Set and orient to the course to be intercepted.

IR.V.A.S4.text: Intercept the specified course at appropriate angle, inbound to or outbound from a navigational facility or waypoint.

IR.V.A.S5.text: Maintain airspeed ±10 knots, altitude ±100 feet, and selected headings ±5°.

IR.V.A.S6.text: Apply proper correction to maintain a course, allowing no more than ¾-scale deflection of the course deviation indicator (CDI). If a distance measuring equipment (DME) arc is selected, maintain that arc ±1 nautical mile.

IR.V.A.S7.text: Recognize navigational system or facility failure, and when required, report the failure to air traffic control (ATC).

IR.V.A.S8.text: Use a multi-function display (MFD) and other graphical navigation displays, if installed, to monitor position, track wind drift, and to maintain situational awareness.

IR.V.A.S9.text: At the discretion of the evaluator, use the autopilot to make appropriate course intercepts, if installed.

IR.V.B.K1.text: Elements related to ATC routes, including departure procedures (DPs) and associated climb gradients; standard terminal arrival (STAR) procedures and associated constraints.

IR.V.B.K2.text: Pilot/controller responsibilities, communication procedures, and ATC services available to pilots.

IR.V.B.R1.text: ATC communications and compliance with published procedures.

IR.V.B.R3.text: Responsibility to use "see and avoid" techniques when possible.

IR.V.B.S1.text: Select, identify (as necessary) and use the appropriate communication and navigation facilities associated with the proposed flight.

IR.V.B.S10.text: Use single-pilot resource management (SRM) or crew resource management (CRM), as appropriate. 14

IR.V.B.S2.text: Perform the appropriate checklist items relative to the phase of flight.

IR.V.B.S3.text: Use the current and appropriate paper or electronic navigation publications.

IR.V.B.S4.text: Establish two-way communications with the proper controlling agency, use proper phraseology, and comply in a timely manner with all ATC instructions and airspace restrictions.

IR.V.B.S5.text: Intercept all courses, radials, and bearings appropriate to the procedure, route, or clearance in a timely manner.

IR.V.B.S6.text: Comply with all applicable charted procedures.

IR.V.B.S7.text: Maintain airspeed ±10 knots, altitude ±100 feet, and selected headings ±10°, and apply proper correction to maintain a course allowing no more than ¾-scale deflection of the course deviation indicator (CDI).

IR.V.B.S9.text: Use displays of digital weather and aeronautical information, as applicable to maintain situational awareness.
